data.why: The repo ships no example PDF, so a small synthetic paper-like PDF with Abstract, numbered sections (1. Introduction, 2. Methods, 2.1/2.2 subsections, 3. Results, 4. Discussion, 5. Conclusion) and a References section was written so the header-detection regexes in section_detector.py have real matches to find.

goals: Upload a paper PDF and get back its Methods section isolated with page range, to hand just that chunk to an LLM instead of the whole paper
Search across extracted section titles and content to locate where a specific topic (e.g. 'dataset' or 'evaluation metrics') is discussed
Sanity-check that a paper's section boundaries and page ranges were detected correctly before trusting the output in a RAG or knowledge-graph pipeline
Export the structured sections as Markdown or JSON for downstream scripts
Browse page-level provenance for a paragraph so a citation can point to the exact source page

review.summary: The tree describes this RAG-prep tool faithfully: upload and segment, check sections, filter by keyword, take a section out. The screens back every claim, and the three features are well cut. Its weak points are that page-range provenance, the tool's main promise, was only tested on a one-page PDF, and several tasks are tester probes or single clicks (empty upload, Debug mode, collapse, case check), so it needs a multi-page re-run and some pruning before filing.
